title: AWS Data Engineering
subtitle: Ingest, transform, govern and analyse data on AWS
audience_line: Data analysts, developers and engineers building data pipelines on AWS
certifications: AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate (DEA-C01), core topics
overview: This programme teaches participants to build data pipelines on Amazon Web Services and covers the core topics of the AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate exam (DEA-C01). They design an S3 data lake with partitioned Parquet and Apache Iceberg tables, ingest batch and streaming data, transform it with AWS Glue and EMR, load and query Amazon Redshift Serverless, govern access and quality with Lake Formation and Glue Data Quality, orchestrate with Step Functions and Amazon MWAA, and analyse results with Athena, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink and QuickSight. Exam practice closes the content, and the programme ends with a final project: an end-to-end data pipeline built and presented by each team.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Data analysts, developers and engineers building data pipelines on AWS

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Core AWS services (course: AWS Cloud Practitioner); Python and SQL (course: Python for Data Science), or equivalent. These are used, not taught

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 27 h: 24 h of chapters + 3 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs on a shared dataset; exam practice

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: One laptop per participant with a browser and the AWS CLI; one AWS sandbox account per team, provided by the organiser, with a budget alert; MWAA and the QuickSight subscription set up by the organiser for the course, Redshift Serverless at minimum base capacity; streams, clusters and warehouses deleted at the end of each lab

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase, practice exam questions and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete the labs and the project

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can build an orchestrated pipeline that ingests, catalogues, transforms, governs and serves data on AWS, and explain its design choices

phases.name: Data Lakes & Ingestion
phases.focus: Lake, warehouse and lakehouse, S3 formats and Iceberg, batch and streaming ingestion
phases.intro: Participants compare batch and streaming, data lakes, warehouses and lakehouses, design an S3 data lake with partitioned Parquet and Apache Iceberg tables, then ingest data with Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, DMS and AppFlow, with an overview of Amazon MSK. Validated lab: a clickstream sent through Kinesis Data Streams and delivered by Firehose into date-partitioned JSON files in the raw zone of the lake.

chapters.title: Data Engineering Fundamentals
chapters.content: Batch vs streaming, data lake vs warehouse vs lakehouse

chapters.title: Storage & Formats
chapters.content: S3 data lake, partitioning, Parquet, Apache Iceberg tables (including Amazon S3 Tables)

chapters.title: Ingestion
chapters.content: Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, DMS, AppFlow, Amazon MSK overview

phases.name: Processing & Warehousing
phases.focus: AWS Glue, EMR, Amazon Redshift Serverless
phases.intro: Participants catalogue and transform the lake with AWS Glue crawlers, the Data Catalog and ETL jobs, see when EMR is the better choice, then design, load and query a Redshift Serverless warehouse. Validated lab: a Glue job that cleans the raw data into a curated Iceberg table, loaded into Redshift Serverless and queried.

chapters.title: Processing
chapters.content: AWS Glue (ETL jobs, crawlers, Data Catalog), EMR

chapters.title: Data Warehousing
chapters.content: Amazon Redshift Serverless design, loading and querying

phases.name: Governance, Orchestration & Analytics
phases.focus: Lake Formation, data quality, Step Functions, MWAA, Athena, Flink, QuickSight
phases.intro: Participants control who sees which data with Lake Formation, check it with Glue Data Quality and trace its lineage, orchestrate the pipeline with Step Functions and Amazon MWAA, analyse it with Athena, Managed Service for Apache Flink and QuickSight, then practise DEA-C01 questions. Validated lab: an orchestrated run that stops when a data quality rule fails, and an analyst role that can query only its permitted columns in Athena.

chapters.title: Governance & Quality
chapters.content: Lake Formation permissions, Glue Data Quality, data lineage (Amazon DataZone / SageMaker Catalog)

chapters.title: Analytics & Streaming Analytics
chapters.content: Athena, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink, QuickSight

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: An end-to-end data pipeline, presented to the group
phases.intro: Teams of two or three build a complete pipeline for a provided dataset, reusing the phase labs, then present it as they would to a data team lead and tear it down.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, ingest with Kinesis and S3, catalogue and transform with Glue, query with Athena

chapters.title: Serve & Orchestrate
chapters.content: Load Redshift Serverless, build the QuickSight dashboard, orchestrate with Step Functions; architecture diagram

chapters.title: Demo & Teardown
chapters.content: Live run of the pipeline, dashboard walkthrough, teardown; questions and feedback

project.title: An End-to-End Data Pipeline on AWS
project.brief: Data ingested with Kinesis and S3, catalogued and transformed with Glue, queried with Athena, loaded into Redshift Serverless and shown on a QuickSight dashboard, the whole run orchestrated by Step Functions and torn down after the demo.
project.stack: AWS: S3, Kinesis Data Streams, Amazon Data Firehose, Glue, Athena, Redshift Serverless, Lake Formation, Step Functions, QuickSight; Python, SQL
project.deliverable: Pipeline code, architecture diagram, dashboard, live demo
